citation.title: Acute Cardiorespiratory and Metabolic Responses to Different Endurance Exercise Modalities in Sedentary College Students Based on Physiological and Perceptual Load Monitoring

population.description: Forty-five sedentary college students (26 men, 19 women) in Beijing, aged 18-26 y, free of mental or cardiovascular disease, muscle injury and medication (self-confirmed; no glucose test, so entered as unselected rather than healthy). Age and BMI are printed only by sex (Table 1: men 23.71 ± 1.88 y, BMI 24.02 ± 1.95; women 22.91 ± 1.79 y, BMI 20.36 ± 1.68); the pooled means and SDs here are computed from those (pooled mean, with between-sex spread added to the within-sex variance), not printed. Completers in the THR condition, the only one entered: 43 (24 men, 19 women); Table 1 means are for all 45.

protocols.name: thr_bout_fasted
protocols.description: Threshold (THR) session of 30 min (Table 2: 5 min warm-up, 20 min continuous at 70-80% HRmax, 5 min cool-down), after a fast of at least 8 h (Methods 2.2: 'required to fast for at least 8 h before each formal exercise session'); n = 43 completers (Results 3: 24 men, 19 women). The bout runs the whole arm, minutes 0 to 30; no run-in is printed, so none is added. Intensity from the measured session-mean VO2 of Table 5 (1.69 L/min), taken as the mean over the whole session (Methods 2.3.2: recorded 'throughout the entire exercise session'; the span the Table 5 mean covers is not printed). Body mass is not printed pooled, so it is derived from Table 1 sex means and this arm's sex counts: (24 x 76.98 + 19 x 55.79) / 43 = 67.62 kg. VO2 = 1.69 x 1000 / 67.62 = 24.99 mL/kg/min; level = (24.99 - 3.7) / 31.7 = 0.6717. Warm-up and cool-down are flattened into the session-mean level. The paper's own Table 6 agrees with this VO2 for THR (TEE 258.52 kcal over 30 min is 8.6 kcal/min against about 8.3 kcal/min from VO2 1.69 L/min; METs 6.63 against 7.1 from VO2 and body mass), unlike its EMR (12.73 kcal/min). 'At least 8 h' is a lower bound, so prefast_hours 8 is assumed; clock hour not printed (08:00 assumed). No food or drink during the bout is mentioned.

findings.description: Mean heart rate during the Threshold (THR) session (whole 30 min) (HRmean, 'Mean Heart Rate in Exercise'), mean of persons

location.where: Table 3, row THR, column HRmean (bpm), mean ± SD

findings.description: Mean respiratory quotient during the Threshold (THR) session (whole 30 min)

location.where: Table 5, row THR, column RQ, mean ± SD

findings.description: Mean respiratory rate during the Threshold (THR) session, mean of persons; the paper's unit 'cpm' (Table 4 column 'RR (cpm)', RR defined as Respiratory Rate) is read as breaths per minute

location.where: Table 4, row THR, column RR (cpm), mean ± SD

left_out.what: HVT, PYT and HIIT bouts (all findings: HR mean and peak, VCO2, RQ). The measured session-mean VO2 (Table 5) that would set their intensity is contradicted by the same paper's Table 6 (TEE over duration, EMR, METs imply VO2 differing by 40 to 150% for HVT, PYT and HIIT), so the intensity is not established; PYT (nine 2-min stages) and HIIT (5 x 2 min sprints with 3 min recovery) are also not steady, and a flat level would misstate them

Peak heart rate (HRpeak, Table 3) for every condition including THR: the mean of each person's highest value over a session with warm-up and cool-down cannot come from the flat session-mean level the model is given (THR mean 160.14, peak 172.11)
VCO2 (Table 5) for THR: mean 1.51 L/min is consistent with VO2 x RQ, but its SD 0.59 cannot be (VO2 SD 0.31, RQ SD 0.02); same for PYT and HIIT

Resting condition (REST) heart rate, VO2, VCO2, RQ, respiratory and energy values (Tables 3 to 6), and resting HR in Table 1 by sex: the paper describes no resting measurement (when, how long, before or after the bouts, n), so no run-in can be stated; REST VO2 0.62 L/min (about 2.6 METs) also contradicts REST METs 1 and EMR 1.54 kcal/min

Energy metabolic rate (kcal/min), METs and total energy expenditure (kcal) per condition (Table 6): EMR for THR (12.73 kcal/min) contradicts the printed VO2 (about 8.3 kcal/min) and TEE/duration (8.6 kcal/min); TEE is cumulative kcal and METs a ratio
Respiratory rate for HVT, PYT and HIIT (Table 4)
Minute ventilation (mL) and tidal volume (mL) per condition (Table 4), and end-tidal O2% and CO2% (Table 5)
HIIT high-intensity-zone and interval-zone heart rate, ventilation and respiratory values (Tables 3 and 4): the timing of the zones within the session is not printed, and no VO2 is printed by zone
Heart rate in the warm-up and cool-down separately, and any time course within a session (Figures 1 to 3 only)
RPE, Feeling Scale, session-RPE, TRIMP (Table 8) and regression/correlation coefficients (Table 7, Figures)
